mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 5.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for three consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals weakening consumer demand and economic stagnation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 is flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals aggressive monetary easing, which supports risk assets and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy and higher interest rates, which depress equity valuations and result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
